claims.text: data-ownership.md: each kind of data has exactly one owner, whose value is right when copies disagree; every other place holds a copy that needs a way to stay fresh or a stated reason why not.
Payments owns payments and refunds in donhang_payments; accounting reconciles against donhang_payments (the old payments table in donhang is a copy nobody updates).
Report figures are up to one hour old plus the run time; each run recomputes the last 3 days (assumed); the review plans a full recompute once a week (assumed) for older changes.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 40-42, 50; docs/design/reporting-design-review.md @ stage-4 line 93

claims.text: Daily totals per shop are not an owner but a copy in the reporting database; each figure's owner stays Ordering (donhang) or Payments (donhang_payments), and those are trusted when they disagree.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/data-ownership.md @ stage-4 line 21; ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 55-56

claims.text: ADR 0028: a daily job in Payments lists each difference between refund rows and the gateway's report for staff; it never changes a refund row; a correction is a new change made by a person.

Driver 3: reports across shops include shops moved to their own database (ADR 0026). Revenue needs donhang and donhang_payments, not joinable in one query; db-replica (Compose profile replica) copies the whole db server, still cannot join them, and has no moved shop's database.
claims.source_hint: reporting-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 19-23, 75-77; ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 15-16, 23-25; data-ownership.md @ stage-4 line 28

claims.text: Driver 2: each shop sees only its own figures. Each summary row carries a shop id; from release 2 shop staff read by the shop taken from the access token, with row-level security as in ADR 0013 (assumed); Đơn Hàng's own team reads all rows.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 43-44; reporting-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 19-22, 47-48, 107

claims.text: The design review's challenge table has five rows: three answered with next step 'none' and no owner; live sales screen: new requirement reopening ADR 0031, record it, product owner; job fails a day: alert when late, Shop team.
If the job fails, figures age, each report still shows the time its figures were last computed, and a rerun recomputes 3 days.

ADR 0031 has two revisit conditions: a requirement for live figures (order messages must then carry amounts); a question daily totals cannot answer in time (then a store for analytic queries on detailed data is needed).
Adding amounts to order messages is a schema change every reader must accept.
ADR 0031's comments section records a backend developer asking why not use db-replica; answered that the replica cannot join two databases and lacks moved shops; decision unchanged.
The Shop team runs the reporting job, database and server (ADR 0025, assumed).

Answering from ownership is right when one disagreeing figure is a copy; when a copy stays wrong after the runs that should fix it, the copy's keeper must explain the drift even though the owner's value still decides.
A refund row marked refunded but missing from the gateway report becomes a difference only after one more run (assumed), and is listed for staff.

The job reads ADR 0026's table of which database holds each shop on every run, not a fixed list, so a moved shop's figures come from its new database at the next run and reports across shops stay complete.
claims.source_hint: reporting-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 50-61; ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 37-39

claims.text: The reporting requirements accept figures up to two hours old (assumed).
Filtering rows only in the screen still sends other shops' rows to the client; filtering where rows are read, by the shop in the access token, keeps them from leaving.

ADR 0031 consequences: a new question daily totals do not answer (e.g. sales per hour) needs a new summary table reloaded from source; the review's risks table lists best-selling products per hour as open, owned by the product owner.
claims.source_hint: reporting-design-review.md @ stage-4 line 95; ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 53-54

beyond_scope: Fifth challenge row (job fails for a day) read from the quoted table; not in the outline items.
What-if on a moved shop reuses the reporting-design deep dive (prereq knowledge), not re-decided.
